title: End-to-end observability playbook for console analytics ingestion and backend services
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Goal: Define, instrument, and roll out an operational playbook that gives end-to-end observability for Console backend services and the usage analytics ingestion pipeline. This includes clear SLIs and SLOs for ingestion and processing, standardized tracing and log enrichment patterns, Grafana dashboards for realtime ops, and runbook playbooks for incidents. Scope excludes long-term cost analytics (handled in Optimize), but must surface unit-cost regressions as alertable signals.

Why: Teams currently lack a single source of truth for analytics pipeline health. Incidents surface late (consumer-facing dashboards show missing metrics) and root cause is often manual investigation across producer services, Kafka/streaming layers, and ETL jobs. This ticket creates measurable SLIs, sampling/tracing rules, and operator-facing dashboards so we detect and resolve regressions faster while avoiding noisy alerts.

High-level deliverables:
- Agree SLIs and SLO targets for key stages: event-acceptance (ingest success rate), pipeline-lag (p95 processing latency), schema-reject rate, downstream-delivery (delivery success to warehouse/consumer), and cardinality error rate.
- Instrument structured logs and trace spans across producers, ingestion gateway, batching layer, transformer, and delivery workers with consistent span names and 5 correlation IDs (request_id, user_id (hashed), org_id, ingestion_batch_id, trace_id).
- Sampling strategy: full traces for errors and p95+ latency, 1% baseline sampling for successful flows; configure adaptive sampling to capture bursts.
- Dashboard set: ops overview, per-tenant ingestion heatmap, slow-path trace explorer, schema errors timeline, and SLA burn-down.
- Alerts and runbooks: actionable alerts with triage steps and rollback/playback instructions.
- Backfill plan: compute baseline metrics for last 90 days to set SLO targets.

Acceptance criteria:
- SLIs are defined and documented in Confluence with numerator/denominator and reporting cadence.
- Instrumentation PRs merged to ingestion-gateway, transform-worker, and delivery-worker repos with tests and 80% unit coverage for new logic.
- Grafana dashboards deployed to ops cluster and linked in runbook.
- PagerDuty alert rules created for SLO breach windows: 15m and 6h.
- Latency p95 measurement available in logs/traces; demo to SRE and PM with sample incident drill.

Out-of-scope: deep-cost attribution, schema-aware replay tooling (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: Documented SLIs/SLOs in Confluence with formulas and reporting windows
Tracing instrumentation merged across ingestion and transformer services
Grafana ops dashboard published and shared with SRE and PM
PagerDuty alerts and runbook entries created and validated via drill

notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive sampling increases cost; we adopted error-first full capture with low baseline sampling to balance cost and fidelity.
We will reuse existing tracing infra (OpenTelemetry -> Jaeger) and extend exporters for high-throughput Kafka message annotations.
If SLO backfills show seasonal variance, we'll propose tiered SLOs per plan (free vs paid) in follow-up PRD.
